records.title: Relativization barrier
records.statement: There are oracles A and B with P^A=NP^A and P^B!=NP^B; a proof that relativizes uniformly cannot resolve the unrelativized question.
hypotheses: The proposed method is shown to relativize in the relevant sense.
records.conclusion: The method class is insufficient by itself.
residual_hypotheses: Nonrelativization is necessary for affected methods but not sufficient for correctness.
records.claim_boundary: A barrier classifies methods; it does not decide P versus NP.

records.title: Natural-proofs barrier
records.statement: Under strong pseudorandomness assumptions, constructive, large and useful properties cannot prove broad general circuit lower bounds of the prohibited form.
hypotheses: The lower-bound property satisfies the exact constructivity, largeness and usefulness conditions.
The activating pseudorandomness assumption is stated.
records.conclusion: The natural proof route is conditionally obstructed.
records.quantifier_scope: the theorem's natural-property and circuit-size regime
records.source_locator: Definitions and main conditional barrier theorem
residual_hypotheses: The barrier is conditional and does not exclude all lower-bound methods.
Failure to be natural is not a proof of usefulness.
records.claim_boundary: Natural proofs is not a universal impossibility theorem.

records.title: Algebrization barrier
records.statement: Many arithmetizing techniques remain valid relative to algebraic extensions of oracles, while oracle worlds separate major class relations; such algebrizing methods cannot settle those relations alone.
hypotheses: The proposed method algebrizes in the defined sense.
records.conclusion: The method class is insufficient by itself.
records.quantifier_scope: the relations classified in the paper
residual_hypotheses: Nonalgebrization is not sufficient for a valid proof.
records.claim_boundary: Escaping algebrization supplies no theorem conclusion by itself.

records.title: Hardness versus randomness
records.statement: Sufficient circuit hardness yields pseudorandom generators and derandomization consequences; in particular, strong hardness for E can imply P=BPP.
hypotheses: The required explicit hardness assumption holds with the specified quantitative strength.
Generator construction and simulation costs match.
records.conclusion: Randomized computation is derandomized in the stated regime.
records.model: uniform randomized algorithms and nonuniform circuit hardness
residual_hypotheses: The required circuit hardness is unproved.
Derandomization does not by itself separate P from NP.
records.claim_boundary: Hardness-versus-randomness transfers are conditional and target randomness, not the canonical class equality directly.

records.title: Cook-Reckhow proof-system interface
records.statement: NP=coNP iff there exists a polynomially bounded propositional proof system in the Cook-Reckhow sense.
hypotheses: Proof systems are polynomial-time verifiable surjections onto tautologies.
Polynomial boundedness concerns shortest proof length.
records.conclusion: Universal polynomial proof length is equivalent to NP=coNP.
residual_hypotheses: NP=coNP is not known equivalent to P=NP.
Lower bounds for every proof system—not one named system—would be required.
records.claim_boundary: Proof complexity targets NP versus coNP unless an additional bridge is supplied.

records.title: Resolution lower bounds
records.statement: Pigeonhole-principle tautologies require exponential resolution proofs.
hypotheses: The formula family and size measure match.
residual_hypotheses: No lower bound is supplied for arbitrary Cook-Reckhow systems or extended Frege.
records.claim_boundary: A lower bound for resolution does not prove NP!=coNP or P!=NP.

records.title: Hardness magnification
records.statement: For selected natural meta-complexity problems and restricted models, modest lower-bound improvements can imply major circuit lower bounds.
hypotheses: The exact magnification theorem, problem, model and threshold are fixed.
The modest lower bound crosses the theorem's threshold.
records.conclusion: A stronger separation follows conditionally from the magnified premise.
records.source_locator: Per-theorem threshold extraction required; 2025 source remains preprint
residual_hypotheses: The threshold lower bound is itself unproved.
Localization and natural-proof interactions remain theorem-specific.
records.claim_boundary: Magnification converts one missing lower bound into another; it does not supply the premise.

records.title: Minimum Circuit Size Problem and meta-complexity boundary
records.statement: MCSP is a natural NP meta-complexity problem, but its NP-hardness under standard reductions and its transfer to P versus NP are delicate and reduction-dependent.
hypotheses: Truth-table encoding, circuit basis, size threshold and reduction type are fixed.
records.conclusion: MCSP may serve as a magnification or barrier testbed under precise reductions.
records.uniformity: uniform decision problem over nonuniform objects
records.quantifier_scope: all truth-table instances under the fixed threshold encoding
records.source_locator: Magnification and non-NP-hardness barrier results; per-reduction extraction required
residual_hypotheses: No accepted standard many-one NP-completeness theorem is supplied.
A bridge from a selected MCSP lower bound to the terminal target must be named.
records.claim_boundary: Meta-complexity resemblance is not an exact equivalence to P versus NP.
